body.intent: Give the controller on-demand access to the exact insrc_* MCP contracts instead of guessing them. Pillar 1 (fully speced here): a new read-only MCP tool `insrc_schema({ tool, phase? })` that returns the exact input JSON schema for any registered insrc_* MCP tool call, read from the SAME schema objects the handlers validate against (server.ts registration + per-step schema.ts modules) — never a hand-maintained copy — so a controller looks up the authoritative message shape rather than guessing and getting rejected. `tool` is required (omitted/unrecognized → non-throwing `{ error, validTools }`). Phase-based tools (insrc_analyze_step, insrc_workflow_step, insrc_review_step, insrc_code_review_step, insrc_build_step, insrc_triage [start/classify], insrc_workflow_run [start/poll]): `phase` omitted → `{ error, validPhases }`; a recognized phase → `{ schema, description, validPhases }` for that phase's static envelope. One-shot tools (insrc_workflow_approve, insrc_docgen, insrc_analyze): `phase` ignored → `{ schema, description }`. Runtime-generated inner payloads get the static envelope only + a `description` pointer to the prior response's inline `schema`. All errors are normal structured responses (`{ error, validTools?, validPhases? }`), never thrown. Pillars 2–3 (the reframe, epic-level direction): apply the same on-demand principle to the STEERING itself — add a parallel on-demand retrieval surface (an `insrc_guide({ workflow })`-style IPC + thin MCP tool) that returns the full per-workflow procedural instructions from the same canonical steering content, and restructure the injected steering block into a thin skeleton (front-door decision tree + a compact catalog of available insrc_* / IPC calls) with the per-workflow detail moved behind the on-demand call. Bundled steering-block content, authored in the canonical src/prompts/steering-block.md so daemon-ctl.sh's steering-refresh propagates it to every registered repo: document insrc_build_step (the only registered tool with zero steering coverage, and the BUILD artifact the completion step references), add a rule to call insrc_schema before emitting an unsure message shape, and add a short dedicated insrc_schema self-entry (call/response shape).
body.scopeBoundary: Pillar 1 (insrc_schema) is fully speced by the recorded decisions and is ready to build. Pillars 2–3 (the insrc_guide-style on-demand steering retrieval + the thin-skeleton steering restructure) are captured as the epic-level direction, not fully designed here: their detailed design is deferred to design.epic/design.story — specifically guide granularity (per-workflow vs per-stage), whether insrc_guide is daemon-IPC-first with a thin MCP wrapper (the docgen pattern) vs MCP-only, and exactly what stays in the thin skeleton vs moves behind the on-demand call. insrc_schema reads live handler schema objects only (never a re-derivation/copy), does not fully type the runtime-generated dynamic inner payloads (defers to the prior response's inline `schema`), and covers registered insrc_* MCP tools only (not other MCP servers' tools). This effort is expected to size as an epic (define → design.epic → stories) covering the three pillars.
nonGoals: insrc_schema is not a re-derivation or hand-maintained copy of tool schemas — it reads the live objects the handlers already validate against.

insrc_schema does not attempt to resolve or fully type the dynamic inner payload of runtime-generated phase responses (workflow_step step/synthesize, analyze_step narrow/bundle, review/code_review/build_step per-turn emissions, workflow_run poll progress) — only the static envelope, deferring to the prior response's own inline `schema` field for that part.
insrc_triage is not grouped with the one-shot tools (workflow_approve, docgen, analyze) — it is phase-based like analyze_step/workflow_step/review_step/code_review_step/build_step.

insrc_workflow_run is not treated as a one-shot tool or left unclassified — it is folded into the phase-based group with 'start' and 'poll' as its two phase names, despite having no literal `phase` field of its own.
insrc_schema's tool coverage is scoped to registered insrc_* MCP tools only, not other MCP servers' tools.

decisions.chosen: Error, listing the valid phase names for that tool
ruledOut: Return only the entry-phase schema (i.e. 'start')
Return a map of ALL phases → schema for that tool in one response
decisions.reason: The tool signature is `{ tool, phase? }` — phase is optional. For a phase-based step tool, what should insrc_schema return when `phase` is omitted?

decisions.chosen: Return the static envelope schema only (e.g. {stepId, response, state} with the dynamic field typed as free-form object), and document that the inline `schema` from the prior response is authoritative for that field's inner shape
ruledOut: Decline for these phases with a pointer message ('this phase's shape is call-specific — use the `schema` field from your last response'), and only serve real schemas for phases with a fully static shape
Aggregate and return the union of every stepId's schema ever registered for that phase, keyed by stepId
decisions.reason: This is the crux call for the feature's actual payoff: most schema-mismatch rejections likely happen on exactly these dynamic-envelope calls (phase:'step'/'narrow'/'synthesize'), so the answer determines whether insrc_schema meaningfully reduces them or only helps the easier, fully-static half of its scope.

decisions.chosen: Schema + orientation metadata — `{ schema, description, validPhases? }` (validPhases included even on a successful phase-scoped lookup, not just on the omitted-phase error)
ruledOut: Raw schema only — `{ schema }`
Schema + a generated minimal example payload conforming to the schema
decisions.reason: Decisions 1 and 2 fixed the omitted-phase error behavior and the dynamic-payload envelope-only rule; this decision is the one remaining piece of the tool's actual output contract for the success path, which nothing so far has pinned down.

decisions.chosen: Require `tool`; error on omitted or unrecognized name, listing all valid insrc_* tool names in the error (same error-lists-valid-options style as the phase-omitted decision)
ruledOut: Treat omitted `tool` as a discovery mode — return the full list of registered insrc_* tool names with one-line descriptions; keep unrecognized name as a hard error
Unify both cases — omitted and unrecognized `tool` both return the same 'valid tool names' payload alongside the description, no hard distinction between 'you forgot' and 'you guessed wrong'
decisions.reason: The signature is `{ tool, phase? }` with `tool` as the lookup key into the registered insrc_* tools. What should insrc_schema do when `tool` is omitted entirely, or given a name that isn't a registered tool?

decisions.chosen: Ignore the extra `phase` and return the tool's single schema as normal

decisions.chosen: Return a normal successful response `{ error: string, validTools?: string[], validPhases?: string[] }` — never throws
ruledOut: Throw a standard MCP tool error (isError:true) with a message string listing the valid tool/phase names
decisions.reason: Per project memory, the daemon's existing `{error}` handlers already frame failures as `result:{error}` rather than throwing (see the ide-artifact-review-panel-epic gotcha) — recommending the option that stays consistent with that established convention.

decisions.chosen: Add a short dedicated steering entry for insrc_schema (name, purpose, `{tool, phase?}` call shape, response shape) alongside the new rule
ruledOut: Fold insrc_schema's description into the existing analyze-tools section (it's a meta/introspection tool, thematically adjacent to insrc_analyze / insrc_analyze_step)

decisions.reason: The steering bundle already adds insrc_build_step docs and a new rule telling controllers to call insrc_schema before guessing a shape. But insrc_schema is itself a brand-new tool — should the same bundle also add a short steering entry documenting insrc_schema's own existence and call shape, or is the new rule's mention of it by name enough for controllers to discover it?

Should insrc_schema instead treat insrc_triage as phase-based, correcting decision 6?

ruledOut: Give it a third, dedicated category ('async-run'): insrc_schema returns both shapes at once, e.g. `{ schema: { start, poll }, description }`, since there are only ever exactly two fixed calls, not an open-ended phase loop

decisions.reason: insrc_workflow_run is an async two-call tool: START returns a runId immediately (input roughly `{ workflow, params, ... }`), and POLL takes a completely different shape `{ poll: runId, cursor }`. It has no `phase` field selecting between them, so it doesn't fit the phase-based bucket as-is, but it also isn't a single fixed shape like the one-shot tools. How should insrc_schema classify and expose it?
